bib.title: TheAgentCompany: Benchmarking LLM Agents on Consequential Real World Tasks

read.skipped: nothing; references skimmed. File is arXiv v3 (10 Sep 2025), not the Dec 2024 original.

question: How well can LLM agents autonomously perform consequential, work-related tasks in a simulated software company?
hypothesis: Current agents can complete simpler tasks but not difficult long-horizon ones; social interaction, complex UIs and private-data tasks are hardest (stated as an argument, not a pre-registered hypothesis).
contributions: A self-hosted, reproducible simulated software-company environment (GitLab, OwnCloud, Plane, RocketChat) with simulated colleagues
175 checkpoint-scored professional tasks across SDE, PM, DS, Admin, HR, Finance and Other
Checkpoint-based partial-credit metrics plus step and cost metrics
Baseline results for twelve LLM backbones with OpenHands and OWL RolePlay agents

method.summary: A benchmark of 175 hand-written tasks in a Dockerised fake software company. Each task has an English intent, weighted checkpoints and Python evaluators (51 tasks also use an LLM judge); simulated colleagues are LLM-backed NPCs on RocketChat. Twelve backbone LLMs are run inside OpenHands CodeAct+Browsing agent, plus OWL RolePlay with GPT-4o and o3-mini.
method.task: long-horizon workplace agent tasks (browsing, coding, terminal, chat with colleagues)

datasets.name: TheAgentCompany
datasets.size: 175 tasks (69 SDE, 28 PM, 14 DS, 15 Admin, 29 HR, 12 Finance, 8 Other)
datasets.split: full set used for every model; no train/dev split
datasets.source: hand-written by 20 co-authors over 2 months (about 3,000 person-hours), referencing O*NET 29.1; environment mock data from real software project data plus curated data

other.also: backs all simulated colleagues (NPCs via Sotopia); fixed across all runs

inference.prompting: OpenHands CodeAct agent with browsing: each step the LLM gets prior history plus current observation and emits a bash, IPython or BrowserGym action; NPC role prompt is described as simple, no prompt engineering

parameters.step_limit: not stated (OWL browsing agent mentioned as failing 'within the step limit')
parameters.interfaces: bash shell, Jupyter IPython server, Playwright Chromium browser with BrowserGym actions
parameters.browser_observation: accessibility tree text plus snapshot (OpenHands is text-based browsing)

other.environment: sandboxed Docker local workspace plus intranet (GitLab, OwnCloud, Plane, RocketChat); VM image also provided
other.judge_coverage: 51 tasks (29%) use LLM evaluation, deterministic keyword match first with LLM fallback
other.npc_cost: inferred: at most $0.024 per NPC interaction under 3000 input and 1000 output token assumption

metrics.name: Success (full completion score S_full)
metrics.definition: 1 if all checkpoints pass, else 0; reported as % of tasks

metrics.name: Score (partial completion score)
metrics.definition: S_partial = 0.5 * Result/Total + 0.5 * S_full, Result = awarded points, Total = points available

metrics.name: Steps
metrics.definition: total number of LLM calls during task execution

metrics.name: Cost per instance
metrics.definition: prompt tokens x prompt price + completion tokens x completion price, assuming no prompt caching

eval.protocol: single pass over all 175 tasks per model; no repeated runs, seeds or confidence intervals reported; no human baseline; Python evaluators plus Claude-3.5-Sonnet LLM judge for 51 tasks

availability.data: environment and tasks released at https://the-agent-company.com; experiments at https://github.com/TheAgentCompany/experiments

evidence.where: Sec 4.1 (formula split across lines in extracted text)
no statement of runs per task; inferred single run from tables reporting one number per model

limits: Tasks lean straightforward because they must be auto-evaluable; no creative tasks such as brainstorming or architecture design (Sec 8).
Only two agent scaffolds (OpenHands CodeAct, OWL RolePlay) tested; others may differ (Sec 8).
No human performance baseline, for cost reasons; humans only checked feasibility (Sec 8, Appendix J).
Task content came from introspection by people familiar with the roles, possibly unlike real enterprise tasks (Sec 8).
Authors caution against inferring job automation risk, since the task list is not exhaustive (Sec 5.2).
Single run per model, no variance, seeds, temperature, step limit or token limits stated; models ran on different OpenHands versions (0.14.2 vs 0.28.1), confounding comparison of newer models.
NPC and LLM judge fixed to Claude-3.5-Sonnet, which is also an evaluated model; no judge-vs-human agreement reported, and Appendix E dismisses judge concerns by assertion.
Per-category counts are small (Finance 12, Other 8, DS 14), so Table 5 differences are noisy.
Models are from 2024 to mid 2025 and have dated.
